applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 8 (often about ages 13-14) onto that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Florida Grade 8 mathematics is grade-coded (MA.8), not Algebra 1 or Geometry. MYP mathematics can be standard or extended. That choice is a school decision and is not made here.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: Grade 8 Florida mathematics (MA.8) is mapped here to the MYP mathematics subject group. The public page names the branches number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, and statistics and probability, and two levels of challenge (standard and extended). It does not place Grade 8 in either level.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Developing and applying these social, thinking, research, communication and self management skills helps students learn how to learn.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP prescribes sixteen key interdisciplinary concepts along with related concepts for each discipline.

official_requirements.text: MYP teachers assess the prescribed subject-group objectives using the assessment criteria for each subject group in each year of the programme.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: In the International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP), mathematics promotes both inquiry and application, helping students to develop problem solving techniques that transcend the discipline and that are useful in the world beyond school.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP mathematics framework encompasses number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: In the MYP, the topics and skills in the framework for mathematics are organized so that students can work at two levels of challenge: standard mathematics and extended mathematics.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The mathematics subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Knowing and understanding; B Investigating patterns; C Communicating; D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 8 Florida mathematics in this draft covers irrational numbers and scientific notation, integer exponents, equivalent expressions, multi-step linear equations and two-step inequalities, equations of the forms x squared equals p and x cubed equals q, slope and linear equations, systems of two linear equations, functions, the Pythagorean Theorem and angle relationships, transformations and similar triangles, bivariate data, and probability of repeated experiments. Those ceilings are Florida's. A reasonable MYP fit is the number, algebra, geometry, and statistics branches, plus criteria A and D, without claiming IB sets the same grade-8 limits or chooses standard versus extended mathematics for this grade.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Defining irrational numbers in the real number system fits the number branch and criterion A. The approximation limit is Florida's.
Scientific notation for very large or very small quantities is a Florida benchmark. The public MYP pages do not name that notation.

Finding real solutions of equations in the forms x²=p and x³=q can sit under criterion A. Those forms, and the limits on p and q, are Florida's. The two spaces before "and" in the Florida file are from the adopted equation objects and are not IB wording.
Interpreting slope and y-intercept in a real-world context fits relationships as an example key concept and criterion D. The slope-intercept form is Florida's.
Deciding whether a relationship is a function, and naming domain and range, is a Florida benchmark. The public mathematics page does not name functions as a branch.
The Pythagorean Theorem fits geometry. The MYP branch name also includes trigonometry, which this Florida grade list does not require.
Theoretical probability of a repeated experiment fits statistics and probability. The repetition limits are Florida's, not a quoted MYP outcome.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
